exposure: Angle of progression (AOP) measured by trans-perineal ultrasound
outcome: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: Nulliparous pregnant women in the active first stage of labour with singleton pregnancy and cephalic presentation were included in the study.
finding: A wider angle of progression (AOP of 121 or more) is associated with vaginal delivery (86.6%), while a narrower angle (AOP of 70 or less) is associated with cesarean section (83.3%).
mod_finding: Wider angle of progression is associated with vaginal delivery and a narrower angle is associated with cesarean section.
cross-section timing: During the active first stage of labour
